STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE FOR BOMB THREAT 
 
1. SHORT BRIEF ON BOMB THREAT  
1.1 While most bomb threats turn out to be hoaxes and most suspicious packages are 
harmless, it is important that all threats and suspicious objects are treated seriously.  
 
1.2 The duty security officers must conduct a preliminary search at the vicinity, to verify if

89f95c0b-58fb-487f-b937-1934ed55d221.text:
1.2 The duty security officers must conduct a preliminary search at the vicinity, to verify if 
there is any suspicious package, believed to be a bomb. However, duty security officers 
will not decide whether to evacuate the premises, that decision should be made by the 
management or Incident Commander. 
 
 
2. CIRCUMSTANCES OF A BOMB THREAT 
2.1. Receiving a bomb threat call / text 
2.2. Receiving / discovering a suspicious article (Letter / Parcel) 
 
 
3. IMPORTANT CONTACTS

4daf9359-0192-47af-842b-cba42dd5975a.text:
2.2. Receiving / discovering a suspicious article (Letter / Parcel) 
 
 
3. IMPORTANT CONTACTS 
3.1 Ensure you have contact information for the following: 
 
Building Manager / Supervisor : _________________________________ 
 
Building Management Office : _________________________________ 
 
Alternate    : _________________________________ 
 
Security Operation Room  : _________________________________

0a951520-c089-4f60-8fa7-d1d22c81d5df.text:
Security Operation Room  : _________________________________ 
 
3.2 In the event of receiving a bomb threat, please use the bomb threat placard and notify 
someone near you or your partner in SCC to call the police immediately.

5b96e8b6-92f2-4d0d-a2dc-0de204de7874.text:

4. PRIOR TO A BOMB THREAT BEING RECEIVED  
4.1 Ensure there is a checklist near all phones. 
 
4.2 Ensure Emergency numbers are near all phones. 
 
4.3 Access controls are enforced to all restricted areas always. 
 
4.4 All areas must ensure a high level of overall housekeeping. 
 
 
5. PROCESS WHEN DISCOVERING A SUSPICIOUS ARTICLE  
5.1. Remain calm and rationale.   
 
5.2. Do not touch, handle, open or submerge it in water.

064a7f98-0ff2-44c3-a4f9-c9c82eb7e831.text:
5.2. Do not touch, handle, open or submerge it in water.    
  
5.3. Immediately switch off your walkie-talkie set and hand phone when near the 
suspicious article.  
 
5.4. Move away from the device to a safe distance (more than 100 meters) to switch on 
and use your communication device to inform you supervisor / management / 
police. It is advisable to use the nearest fixed or land-line telephone instead.

82142821-6110-4d2a-b8ed-66c071701fc8.text:
police. It is advisable to use the nearest fixed or land-line telephone instead.   
 
5.5. Immediately cordon the area at least 100 meters in radius around the device and 
post danger sign boards to keep people away.    
5.6. Remain at the cordoned off perimeter until the arrival of the police. Brief the police 
and provide all information on the incident.  
 
5.7. Record all decisions, details of authorities and other important facts related to the

7a34d5e6-02d2-4c87-8859-895a7a6cf183.text:
5.7. Record all decisions, details of authorities and other important facts related to the 
incident, especially decision on evacuation and communicate to all persons on 
duty.

6. PROCESS WHEN RECEIVING A LETTER / PARCEL BOMB 
   
6.1. Most letter / parcel bombs delivered through the mail or regular courier service will 
tolerate a fair amount of handling. If you receive or someone hands over a letter / 
parcel suspected of containing explosive or biochemical material, do not attempt to 
open it. Most bombs are designed to detonate when the outer wrapping or envelope

99d685d7-7195-4b88-98e0-dd43347a42a7.text:
open it. Most bombs are designed to detonate when the outer wrapping or envelope 
is cut or torn open. You must immediately take the following course of actions:   
 
6.1.1. Switch off walkie-talkie set and hand phone immediately. 
 
6.1.2. Inform the management / call the police  using the nearest fixed or land -line 
telephone.  
 
6.1.3. Place the suspected letter/parcel in the corner of the room away from the window.

45e61882-a8b3-4239-aa87-785bf4b79932.text:
6.1.3. Place the suspected letter/parcel in the corner of the room away from the window.   
 
6.1.4. Evacuate the room or building if necessary, leaving all doors and windows open if 
it is a suspected bomb but close all doors and windows if it is a suspected biohazard 
item.   
 
6.1.5. Secure the premises by putting up a cordon tape and danger signs at least 100 
meters around the perimeter of the suspicious letter / parcel.

997f8fc6-db6a-4cbb-9ae7-41a908c4a5c2.text:
meters around the perimeter of the suspicious letter / parcel. 
   
6.1.6. Instruct everyone not to touch anything that looks suspicious. 
 
6.1.7. Remain at the cordoned off perimeter until the arrival of police.   
 
6.1.8. If an explosion occurs and evacuation is affected, direct evacuees to safer / 
alternative routes of escape.

7. WHEN A BOMB THREAT CALL IS RECIEVED (THROUGH TELEPHONE) 
 
7.1. Treat all bomb threat call real and seriously.  
 
7.2. Remain calm, do not panic, and prolong the conversation with the caller.  
 
7.3. Alert colleague by flashing a bomb threat placard to notify management and police. 
Listen carefully and try to gather as much information as possible with the provided

c33b2ce0-b591-404e-90ea-08d31129a037.text:
Listen carefully and try to gather as much information as possible with the provided 
bomb threat checklist. Refer to Appendix B; BOMB THREAT CHECKLIST 
 
7.4. Take note of which line the call came in on order to access phone records to obtain the 
number of the perpetrator and if possible, record the conversation. 
 
7.5. If the caller puts down the phone, do not place the receiver on the phone hook.

380892f1-ece9-4104-99f7-4e12a8675cfe.text:

Standard Operating Procedure – Bomb Threat 
 
8. WHEN A BOMB THREAT CALL IS RECEIVED (THROUGH TEXT MESSAGE) 
8.1. Screenshot the message received (as evidence for police). 
 
8.2. Remain calm and do not panic and do not delete the message. 
 
8.3. If the number of the caller is displayed, make a call. 
 
8.3.1. If someone picks up, refer to Point 6. When a bomb threat call is received 
(through telephone).

14da3dab-dbae-4a06-9a5f-a1f8b6f65395.text:
(through telephone).  
8.3.2. If the caller does not pick up the phone, reply to the message and try to 
obtain information from the sender on:   
• The precise location of the bomb  
• Exactly how it looks like 
• Time of detonation and what will set it off 
• The amount and type of explosive used 
• The reason for such an act 
• Person or authority that this message should be conveyed to. 
 
8.3.3. If no number is displayed, call police / inform management.

dcd3ad90-dd18-4200-9f3f-9db0c923b1c4.text:
8.3.3. If no number is displayed, call police / inform management. 
 
8.3.4. Be polite, remain calm and do not antagonize or taunt the sender in any way. 
 
8.3.5. Take snapshots or images of the conversation or message as evidence to 
police.

9. RESPONSE ACTION TO THE BOMB THREAT 
 
9.1. The information gathered from a Bomb Threat could generally be classified as 
follows: 
9.1.1. Specific: Where a positive and specific threat has been made and which permits 
the identification of an actual target.   
9.1.2. Non-specific: Where the threat is vague, leaving doubts on its authenticity or 
made in circumstances suggestive of a box.

a98e6bfa-a3c1-46e4-be8e-34cd1df75017.text:
made in circumstances suggestive of a box.   
 
9.2. The response action required to be taken depending on the classification of the 
information would be:  
9.2.1. Temporary suspension of operation in the areas affected. 
 
9.2.2. Evacuation of the building/area where explosive risks are very high or where a 
suspected article is located.   
 
9.2.3. Isolation of the building/area where there are reasonable grounds to believe

bb0da24a-df83-4bb0-9bdf-2173ea7ab782.text:
9.2.3. Isolation of the building/area where there are reasonable grounds to believe 
that an explosive device had been planted to minimize casualty risks.   
 
9.2.4. Conduct a search of the area in an attempt locate the explosive device.   
 
 
10.  SEARCH PROCEDURE TO CONFIRM THE PRESENCE OF BOMB 
10.1. All bomb threat situations will require a search operation.  This would require the 
involvement of all personnel, namely:

40b7f73b-dfa6-4a07-8627-f2762e1be9f3.text:
involvement of all personnel, namely:  
 
10.2. Employees are to search of their immediate work area to determine the presence 
of any potentially dangerous infiltrated package / device. 
 
10.3. Management / Security search by security personnel in other mainly potential 
bomb planting areas, such as reception lobbies, corridors, restrooms, toilets, an 
external portion of the building, etc.

11.  STEPS TO BE TAKEN IMMEDIATELY AFTER INCIDENT 
 
11.1. Panic and fear are natural reactions after a blast. It is usually the duty of the security 
staff upon approval by the building management to still attempt to affect an 
evacuation of the occupants to a pre -determined location (assembly area), away 
from the building and in a pre -determined safe and orderly manner to wait for the

3dd8b092-df67-4b81-b70a-a9925a51d700.text:
from the building and in a pre -determined safe and orderly manner to wait for the 
arrival of the Police and SCDF units. When doing so, you must:   
 
11.1.1. Beware of the unsound structure such as:   
• Collapsed walls   
• Overhanging slabs   
• Buckled columns or beams  
• Crates in the ground   
• Shattered glass panels   
 
11.1.2. Also, watch out for:  
• Secondary fires due to the heat of the explosion   
• Water and gas leaks due to damage from utility pipes

095d5870-ab96-4294-be02-39a595bc598b.text:
• Water and gas leaks due to damage from utility pipes  
• Exposed live electrical wires/cables  
• If all the pre-determined evacuation routes are unsafe, consider leaving the 
occupants where they are until conditions improve. 
11.2. Do not attempt to rescue people inside a collapsed building or move fatalities.   
 
11.3. Do not light matches, candles, or other fires.   
 
11.4. Give first aid to people who are injured if possible.

36ced525-aee1-4bcb-8f28-6321e7bd4c7a.text:
11.4. Give first aid to people who are injured if possible.  
 
11.5. Inform the authorities on known locations of any trapped occupants.   
 
11.6. Cordon off the area and do not enter the building until it has been declared safe.  
 
11.7. Gather and provide details of those who can give information as witnesses to the 
Police.  
 
11.8. Retrieve and provide all data or footage on identities and particulars of occupants

5f9d5789-974e-4321-a991-74103ee1b223.text:
11.8. Retrieve and provide all data or footage on identities and particulars of occupants 
that maybe captured by the security system (CCTV video recording) and the 
entry/exit register record books.

5327c05c-056b-4bfe-8e9d-9231018177e4.text:

11.9. Assist the SCDF by complying with their instructions during the firefighting and 
rescue operations   
   
12.  CROWD CONTROL PROCEDURES (DURING EVACUATION) 
 
12.1. When the decision is made to evacuate (through the Public -Address announcement 
and the second continuous ringing of the fire alarm bells at all floors for 2 minutes) 
either several floors of a larger building, or an entire facility due to a bomb threat,

4cb44cdb-5399-4d2c-8d1e-fc263e91bf47.text:
either several floors of a larger building, or an entire facility due to a bomb threat, 
extreme care must be taken to not cause panic among employees and customers / 
visitors.  
 
12.2. If panic begins, and takes over, the potential for serious personal injury and property 
damage increases dramatically. It is imperative that personnel maintain their 
discipline, evacuate the facility in a calm manner, and proceed to an area where they 
will not be at risk.

04330ba6-e481-44b6-89b9-a9cc68d8600b.text:
will not be at risk.  
 
12.3. Do not allow anyone to run, or rush in the stairwells. Crowd panic can turn a minor 
emergency into a deadly situation.  
 
12.4. If within the minds of the people present in the facility, an emergency does exist, the 
authority to act should be vested in the highest titled person present, e.g. manager. 
This chain of authority should begin at the official levels and continue down via the 
managers and supervisors.

020f9906-62ab-43fb-b0bb-491d168f9236.text:
managers and supervisors.   
 
12.5. Designated ground floor fire exit staircases are to be manned to guide occupants to 
the designated assembly area. 
 
12.6. All main entrances and exits to the building are to be manned to prevent unauthorized 
entry.  
 
12.7. Patrolling frequency of the vicinity is to be increased. 
 
12.8. Direct the Civil Defence Officer upon his arrival to the Fire Command Centre (FCC).

bc619f1f-3f46-4ac4-b780-c9d6aea70672.text:
12.8. Direct the Civil Defence Officer upon his arrival to the Fire Command Centre (FCC). 
 
12.9. Perform traffic control to facilitate the movement of evacuees at points where they 
need to cross roads to get to the assembly area.  
 
12.10. Assist in monitoring the building evacuation status at the assembly area.

13 TRAFFIC CONTROL PROCEDURES (DURING EVACUATION) 
 
13.1. In an event where a large gathering of people or crowd is expected, it is highly possible 
that there will be a large number of vehicles conveying people to the event. This can result in 
the surge of vehicle movement. 
 
13.2. If the security personnel conducting traffic control do not have the necessary knowledge

13.2. If the security personnel conducting traffic control do not have the necessary knowledge 
and skills in executing their roles and responsibilities, this will result in chaos, accidents , and 
another incident. 
 
13.3. Security personnel must adhere to the organizational procedures in dealing with traffic 
control. The procedures may include details such as: 
 
13.3.1. Traffic control is to be provided at various locations, such as, narrow road

segments, intersections, and starting or ending points. Only properly trained or 
certificated personnel are to handle the traffic control responsibilities. 
 
13.3.2. Traffic controllers shall wear reflective gloves and vests before commencement 
of duties. 
 
13.2.3.  Advance warning signs shall be placed, well in advance of the event and any

30dc9b3d-84f2-41fe-bb60-af7a37348209.text:
of duties. 
 
13.2.3.  Advance warning signs shall be placed, well in advance of the event and any 
personnel, to alert oncoming vehicles of the supplemental traffic control and 
the event. 
 
12.2.4.  Traffic controllers will avoid delays or back up of traffic such that 
a “grid-lock” does not happen, waiting times does not exceed two minutes and 
adjacent driveways to neighbouring businesses and residences will not be 
blocked.

f481d844-0f1f-4ce9-a238-34e2525ad756.text:
adjacent driveways to neighbouring businesses and residences will not be 
blocked. 
 
 
12.2.5. To provide advance notification to the residents in the vicinity of the proposed 
Special Event, by any media (newspaper advertisement, flyer, mail, posting of 
signs, etc.), that they may experience some inconvenience or traffic delay during 
the event. 
 
12.2.6. Compliance with all laws; follow the Rules of the Road and regulations.
